resources.string: Everything your navigation app needs — without giving up your privacy.
Nostr road events (speed cameras, hazards, traffic)
Lightning Network tips for event reporters
No account required — no tracking, ever
For maximum privacy — road reports are propagated through the Nostr network — using a VPN is recommended. Mullvad, payable in Bitcoin, is the recommended choice.
Optional — connect to report road events, confirm alerts and earn Lightning tips.
Connect with the Amber signer app. Your private key never leaves Amber.
Paste your private key. Stored in the Android Keystore.
Invalid nsec key — please check and try again.
You are about to rawdog your Nostr private key directly into an app. Anyone with physical or remote access to your device could read it and permanently take control of your Nostr identity.
✦ The safe method is Amber (NIP-55): the nsec never leaves the app signer vault.

Optional: your saved favorites can sync across your devices through the Nostr relays, end-to-end encrypted (NIP-44) with your own key — relays only ever see ciphertext, and nobody but you can read the contents. Enable it anytime from Settings.
Choose whether other Roadstr users see your Nostr name, npub and picture.

Roadstr always publishes the Nostr public key needed to verify a report. In pseudonymous mode, other Roadstr users see only a generic avatar and “nostrich”; in public mode, they also see your Nostr name, npub and profile picture. Your reports, locations, reputation and received zaps remain public on Nostr.
Configure location access and optional voice guidance.

Grant Precise location (not Approximate) while using Roadstr in:
Settings → Apps → Roadstr → Permissions → Location

Roadstr uses a foreground navigation service and does not require permanent background-location access.
Download the 82 MB Kokoro AI model for on-device voice
You can also download the voice model later from\nSettings → Navigation voice.
Roadstr will now open the map.\nYou can configure everything else in Settings.

Roadstr is an experimental, open-source, community-maintained navigation app based on OpenStreetMap data and the Nostr protocol, made available for use in any country. By downloading, installing or using this app, the user unconditionally accepts all of the following terms, without limitation of territory:

🚗 ROAD SAFETY FIRST
The driver must always keep their eyes on the road and comply with all applicable traffic laws and posted signage, which always take precedence over any instruction from the app. Never operate the device while driving; secure it in an approved, visible mount before setting off, and never divert attention from the road to interact with it while the vehicle is moving.

Roadstr is provided strictly "AS IS" and "AS AVAILABLE", without any warranty of any kind, whether express, implied, or statutory — including, without limitation, warranties of accuracy, completeness, reliability, availability, merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement. Map data, routing, speed limits, speed cameras, and restricted-traffic-zone (ZTL/ZAC/LTZ) information come from open, community-maintained sources (OpenStreetMap, Overpass API) that may be incomplete, outdated, or inaccurate for any country, region, or municipality, at any time and without notice. The user is solely responsible for independently verifying, before and during travel, the legality and accessibility of any suggested route against official local signage and regulations.

🗺️ ROUTING COMES FROM OPENSTREETMAP, NOT FROM ROADSTR
Roadstr does not create or maintain any map or road data. Every route, turn, and road surface it suggests comes from OpenStreetMap, a map anyone can edit, interpreted by third-party routing engines that Roadstr does not operate. Roadstr is not responsible for a route that turns out to be illegal, closed, unpaved, unsafe, impassable, or otherwise unsuitable for the user's vehicle — including any "avoid unpaved roads" or similar routing preference, which is a best-effort steer by the routing engine, never a guarantee. Before following any suggested route, especially outside a city or in an unfamiliar area, the user must judge for themselves whether the road ahead can be safely driven by their vehicle, and turn back or choose another way when it cannot.

📍 ACCURACY & GPS
GPS positioning may be inaccurate or unavailable. All directions, distances, and alerts are provided for guidance only and must never be relied upon as the sole basis for a driving decision.

🔒 PRIVACY AND NETWORK SERVICES
Roadstr runs no first-party servers or analytics, but it is not an offline app. When relevant features are used, coordinates or coarse areas and the IP address are sent directly to third parties: routing providers (origin, destination and waypoints), OpenStreetMap/Nominatim/Overpass (search, reverse geocoding, POIs, restricted zones, limits and cameras), Open-Meteo (rounded coordinates), map-tile servers and Nostr relays (city-level geohash). A road report publishes its exact position, time, content and public key to Nostr and is pseudonymous, not anonymous. Favorites and parking remain local unless explicitly exported or synced.
